steps.name: Require every mandatory suite to succeed
steps.run:
python3 - <<'PY'
import json
import os
import sys

required = os.environ["REQUIRED_JOBS"].split()
try:
    needs = json.loads(os.environ.get("NEEDS_JSON", ""))
except ValueError:
    needs = None
valid = (
    bool(required)
    and len(set(required)) == len(required)
    and isinstance(needs, dict)
    and set(needs) == set(required)
    and all(
        isinstance(needs.get(job), dict)
        and needs[job].get("result") == "success"
        for job in required
    )
)
print("All mandatory jobs succeeded" if valid else "::error::Mandatory jobs did not all succeed")
sys.exit(0 if valid else 1)
PY

steps.name: Unit-file / IaC scan + check-mode + scratch-credstore + upgrade contract
Switch / rollback fixture proof (atomic current flip, paired record)
steps.run:
ROOT="$RUNNER_TEMP/opt-qmx"
mkdir -p "$ROOT"
uv run python qmn/deploy/switch.py node-switch \
  --commit aaaaaaaa --config-version cfg-a \
  --fixture-root "$ROOT" --out "$RUNNER_TEMP/switch-a.json"
uv run python qmn/deploy/switch.py node-switch \
  --commit bbbbbbbb --config-version cfg-b \
  --fixture-root "$ROOT" --out "$RUNNER_TEMP/switch-b.json"
uv run python qmn/deploy/switch.py node-rollback \
  --fixture-root "$ROOT" --out "$RUNNER_TEMP/rollback.json"
python - <<'PY'
import json, os, pathlib
root = pathlib.Path(os.environ["RUNNER_TEMP"]) / "opt-qmx"
current = root / "current"
assert current.exists() or current.is_symlink(), current
if current.is_symlink():
    commit = pathlib.Path(os.readlink(current)).name
else:
    commit = current.read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip()
assert commit == "aaaaaaaa", commit
record = json.loads((root / "deployments" / "aaaaaaaa.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
assert record["commit"] == "aaaaaaaa"
assert record["config_version"] == "cfg-a"
assert (root / "trees" / "aaaaaaaa").is_dir()
assert (root / "trees" / "bbbbbbbb").is_dir(), "previous tree must stay recoverable"
print("switch/rollback fixture proof ok")
PY

steps.name: Scope the tree and declare our own package names
steps.run:
python - <<'PY' >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
import pathlib
import sys
import tomllib

root = pathlib.Path(".")
config = tomllib.loads((root / "pyproject.toml").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
excluded = set(config["tool"]["skylos"]["exclude"])

# CLOSE THE ONE HOLE IN THE EXCLUDE LIST - surgically.
#
# Skylos honours [tool.skylos].exclude everywhere except one place: the
# prompt-injection pass ALSO probes a hard-coded set of high-priority
# locations - "", "docs", "prompt(s)", "config(s)", ".github", ".continue" -
# for AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md / README.md and friends, and that probe reads no
# exclude list at all (skylos/analyzer.py). That is why docs/AGENTS.md was
# flagged CRITICAL with "docs" sitting in the exclude list. Passing --exclude
# on the CLI changes nothing: it feeds the very set the probe ignores. Only
# removing the file from this checkout binds.
#
# Round 2 deleted the whole excluded trees, and that was too blunt: the
# diff-aware AI-defect rules read git, not the working tree, so wiping adws/
# read as "every CLI flag in adws was deleted in this diff" and invented 51
# SKY-A104 findings. So we delete only what the probe can actually reach - the
# agent-instruction basenames inside excluded trees. Today that is exactly one
# file, and it is markdown, so no diff-aware rule has anything to say about it.
#
# Coupled to skylos==4.33.2 (pinned above). If a later version widens that
# probe, the leak returns as a visible CI failure, never as a silent hole.
# Safe by construction: this checkout is disposable and nothing is pushed from
# this job (persist-credentials: false, permissions contents: read).
probe_names = {
    "readme.md", "readme.rst", "readme.txt", "security.md",
    "contributing.md", "contributing.rst", "prompt.md", "prompts.md",
    "prompts.yaml", "prompts.yml", "agents.md", "claude.md",
    ".cursorrules", ".clinerules", ".windsurfrules",
}
for name in sorted(excluded):
    tree = root / name
    if not tree.is_dir():
        continue
    for candidate in sorted(tree.rglob("*")):
        if candidate.is_file() and candidate.name.lower() in probe_names:
            candidate.unlink()
            print(f"removed from scan: {candidate.as_posix()}", file=sys.stderr)

# DECLARE our own importable names.
#
# The dependency-hallucination rule (SKY-D222) resolves every import root
# against PyPI and calls anything missing a hallucination. It only counts a
# name as local when it sits at the repository root, so this workspace's
# namespace packages (packages/*/src/qmf) and the top-level tool modules that
# the pytest pythonpath exposes are invisible to it. They are first-party and
# deliberately never published, so we name them - which teaches the rule our
# vocabulary and leaves it fully armed for everything else.
# */src covers top-level apps (qmb/, qml/, qmn/); */*/src covers
# packages/*/src and extensions/*/src. Deeper trees (e.g. qmx-agents)
# stay on the floor set below until their layout is stable.
namespaces = {
    child.name
    for src in list(root.glob("*/src")) + list(root.glob("*/*/src"))
    for child in src.iterdir()
    if child.is_dir() and not child.name.startswith((".", "_"))
}
tool_modules = {
    module.stem
    for module in root.glob("tools/*.py")
    if not module.stem.startswith("_")
}
# A floor for namespaces that later epics introduce, so the first commit that
# adds one cannot re-trip this before its src/ tree exists.
floor = {"qmf", "qmb", "qml", "qmn", "qma"}
allow = sorted(namespaces | tool_modules | floor)
print(f"first-party names: {allow}", file=sys.stderr)
print("SKYLOS_PRIVATE_DEPS_ALLOW=" + ",".join(allow))
PY

steps.name: Scan
steps.run:
set +e
# -a is the full local audit: dead code + security/dangerous flow +
# secrets + quality + dependency CVEs + the evidence-backed AI-defect
# checks. Scope and exclusions come from [tool.skylos] in pyproject.toml,
# so this command is the same one a developer runs locally.
python -m skylos.cli . -a --no-upload --json > skylos-report.json
status=$?
set -e
# 0 = clean, 1 = findings (the Gate step below is what decides). Any
# other code means the run itself broke, and a fail-closed gate must
# never read a broken run as a clean one.
if [ "$status" -ne 0 ] && [ "$status" -ne 1 ]; then
  echo "::error::Skylos scan exited $status; refusing to treat that as a clean result"
  exit "$status"
fi

steps.name: Annotate the commit and PR
steps.run: python -m skylos.cli cicd annotate --input skylos-report.json --max 50 || true
